wallpaper.editPrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / compositing.
EDIT TARGET is input image 1: the finished 16:9 forest-green portrait wallpaper with four small photographic prints on the right.
Make ONLY this requested change: SWAP THE POSITIONS of the two specific framed photo prints identified by inputs 2 and 3.
Input 2 is identification/reference: the long dark-haired green-tinted close-up selfie with a small cross-shaped hair clip, currently the UPPER-RIGHT small framed print.
Input 3 is identification/reference: the silver compact-camera photo with a glasses-wearing portrait on the camera LCD, currently the LOWER-RIGHT framed print over the striped sleeve.
Move the CAMERA print to the previous upper-right selfie position among the flowers.
Move the GREEN-TINTED LONG-HAIR SELFIE print to the previous lower-right camera position over the outer sleeve.
Swap the whole photographic paper objects, not just the faces. Retain their own image contents, narrow aged-ivory matte-paper borders and convincing subtle contact shadows. Small scale/rotation adjustments are allowed only to fit the two existing spots elegantly, so every frame remains fully inside the canvas and the lower print leaves about 4-5% bottom margin. Minor paper-border overlap is fine; do not cover any small-photo face.

Strict invariants: do NOT change the large main person's face, expression, skin, hair, pose, clothing or size. Preserve the entire left 40% dark negative space, the flower background everywhere outside the two swap spots, the warm analog grain/color grading, and the other TWO small prints (black-dress/manga at upper-right-left, glasses-wearing yellow-blouse/exhibition at mid-right) in exactly their existing positions. Keep exactly FOUR small framed prints, each photo exactly once. No duplicate photos, no new people, no new objects, no new captions, watermarks, recording overlays, timestamps, countdowns, particles, text or UI.
Do not redesign or recompose the wallpaper. Do not invent replacement faces. This is a localized swap of two existing paper photos only.
Output the wallpaper itself, no mockup. Maintain exact landscape 16:9 composition. Target final file dimensions 2560x1440.

petals.origin: Built-in image generation, 1254x1254 RGBA 2x2 sprite atlas. Transparent corner/center alpha verified.
petals.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: transparent particle sprite atlas for a subtle photographic flower-garden desktop wallpaper.
Create a square 2 by 2 sprite sheet containing exactly FOUR separate natural flower-petal cutouts, exactly one centered in each quadrant, with generous truly transparent empty gutters and a transparent outer margin. There is no visible grid. Each petal occupies at most 55 percent of its quadrant's width and height. No overlap, no touching quadrants, no cast shadow onto any background.
Top-left: one curved ivory-white rose petal, soft warm pale pink at the base, slightly curled organic edge, viewed from above at a slight angle.
Top-right: one small dusty-blue hydrangea petal, single petal, natural delicate veins, viewed slightly obliquely.
Bottom-left: one pale blush-pink rose petal, translucent edges, gentle irregular natural fold.
Bottom-right: one small creamy-white hydrangea petal with a subtle cool-blue tint near its base, a different angle from the others.
Real macro photographic detail, delicate satin botanical surface, subdued light, restrained cream/blush/dusty blue palette. These will be rendered at only 12 to 32 pixels on screen over an existing forest-green portrait photograph, so make clean distinct realistic silhouettes. Actual transparent alpha, not a checkerboard image or solid background.
No text, labels, borders, leaves, stems, whole flowers, multiple petals inside one quadrant, decorative sparkles or logos. Square atlas, equal 2x2 quadrants.
